findings.reason: Schema-detach requests and decisions, capture provider/store before any lookup or persistence await, then dispatch the validated copy.
CLI route/acquire/renew cap TTL at7200; full route lease construction validates before arbitration. Local acquire/renew/release reject invalid input before physical lock or state creation.

Persist the complete resolved original profile tuple for provider/harness/identity-only preferences. Historical partial targets never borrow selected fallback fields. Real catalog planner-to-replay checks prefer latest original evidence over older unattributed stops.

A tagged capacity refusal commits future timestamp normalization; installed SDK maps it to the bounded existing capacity error. Admitted SQL test combines10000 future rows, capacity refusal, body/ID preservation, durable normalized timestamps and later expiry/admission; concurrent9999 boundary admits exactly one.
Retain metadataSchema.parse output before waiting; mutable holder and toJSON hooks cannot corrupt diagnostic sidecars. Physical SQLite authority unchanged.

Launch held-lock fixture using the actual Node vite-node entrypoint, avoiding a pnpm wrapper. Ordinary crash cleanup now has strict zero-rescue posture; independent GUARD owner-death positive controls remain unchanged. Earlier R1 assertion that tagging this fixture establishes deterministic rescue is superseded.

Real project quota, organization spend, model token and unattributed identity stops remain conservative for matching provider/harness where narrower exclusion cannot be proved. Explicit identity must match; all session-bound evidence is excluded from new routes. Latest known expired classification releases authority without resurrecting older evidence. Source-grounded R2 dissent corrects R1 overbroad scope exclusion.

optional_dispositions.reason: SQL future full inbox is an EC violation; repaired transaction-preserving refusal.
ENOTDIR and ELOOP inspection uncertainty quarantine only the prepared key; parent-file regression permits unrelated mutations.
Invalid local mutation inputs refuse before lock creation, aligned with SDK validation.
Null cursor is already rejected by SQL validation; the unreachable predicate grants no authority. Removing it would only be optional cleanup.
Retry-After docs explicitly name IMF-fixdate, with no new obsolete-date contract.
Persisted classification ledger itself is asserted free of the synthetic secret.
Own-property lookup ignores inherited active counts for a legal constructor profile.

findings.reason: Omit only null optional envelope fields; preserve every nested body null. Admitted SQL compares mixed env/PATH/null body and parses the complete returned SDK page.
Recognize CR, LF, U+2028 and U+2029 as JavaScript multiline starts, with case-sensitive ENV semantics and retained-inbox digest controls.
Use ASCII C-collated word boundaries and case semantics, preserving punctuation-ending and Unicode-lookalike safe metadata.
Translate exactly the JavaScript whitespace class for case-insensitive lexical safety patterns; keep original text for private-key/AWS and ENV patterns.

Validate encoded JSON syntax with PostgreSQL json, tokenize and validate number finiteness separately, normalize numeric tokens and active NUL/surrogate escapes only in the temporary guard tree. Preserve escaped-backslash parity and original persisted strings. Recursively validate decoded keys and values rather than skipping valid JSON on jsonb representability errors.
Nonempty holder validation and null-safe SQL equality precede expiry or mutation.
Self-holder absence proof requires actual host, PID and alive liveness together.
Classified path/Git uncertainty retains the pending key and permits unrelated mutations; shared persistence failures still propagate.
Future-clock normalization is persisted under lock before capacity refusal, preserving retained messages for later expiry.
Null-prototype dictionaries survive mutations and all aggregate counts remain safe integers.
Requests are schema-detached before awaiting; authoritative registry and mutation publication serialize schema output only.
Pending pre-append session/turn dependency IDs seed the existing DATA closure, including session ancestors.
Provider/harness/identity/session/task and supported scope checks occur before any cooldown, adaptive, fallback, override or publication effect.
Latest applicable evidence wins; known expired classifications lose all live policy authority without resurrecting older classifications.
A refused preliminary route returns before state initialization, arbitration or record publication.
SQL cursor validation uses null-safe type checks on both required named keys; installed-SDK and local pages use returned timestamps/IDs.
Only nonnegative safe integer delays establish wait authority; invalid evidence falls back to bounded integer exponential delay, and unsafe Retry-After is ignored.
Ownership and terminal settlement use the session/turn tuple, with independent duplicate settlement controls.
The intentional lock-holder death test declares the existing owner-death control; strict rescue-count and quiescence validation remain unchanged.

Selected the explicitly offered documentation/compatibility option: no in-place adoption or new legacy renew/release/expiry takeover; operators stop/prove old holders and use a fresh root and disjoint paths. Existing acquisition/cooldown/inspection behavior remains, with map-key corruption checks.
Normal release, stale recovery and cleanup reconciliation retain actual DATA causes and actors; removal-before-marker crash is recovered using prepared durable intent.
Missing acceptance evidence is still a merge gate, never waived. Source-bound hosted full verification, rehearsal, current producer audit, exact candidate reviews and post-merge CI are required.

The documented IMF HTTP-date and complete integer forms are supported; obsolete RFC850/asctime formats are not newly claimed.

findings.reason: Opus partial output identified PostgreSQL54001 on malformed deeply nested ordinary text. Independent local reproduction also demonstrated a safe deeply nested duplicate member overwritten by a later value. Existing reader accepts both, while surviving valid deep metadata must reject. Only after PostgreSQL program_limit_exceeded, an iterative JSON grammar validator validates the entire original input, including deep subtrees; malformed JSON stays ordinary text. Valid composites beyond effective depth64 become temporary existing error markers in bounded inspection input. Original lexical checks and bodies remain unchanged. Existing Unicode normalization and JSONB last-member resolution then discard overwritten deep branches; surviving depth violations reject before mutation. No unconditional acceptance/refusal of54001, stack setting changes, new public limits, functions, signatures, privileges or frozen-contract edits.

Validate and detach the complete request before effects, then sample the default clock inside the acquired physical lock. Explicit request.now is captured and retained. Real lock contention with TTL1 now grants a live lease and refuses an immediate competing hard acquisition.

Local and installed-SDK send share input fields from the existing frozen coordination contract and detach metadata before effects. SQL directly validates sender/type/scope/optional IDs/body before locking, normalization and pruning. Malformed requests leave local state absent, make zero SDK fetches, and preserve admitted SQL inbox bytes including a future-dated row; valid following requests remain readable.

optional_dispositions.reason: Astra correctness demonstrated a stale default acquisition clock. Sampling after physical acquisition restores lease lifetime.

Persisting the resolved original profile tuple provides original-target replay context even without explicit preference overrides. It does not grant identity or accounting authority; no regression demonstrated.

Historical partial targets cannot establish original provider/harness/identity context. Refusing to borrow a selected fallback tuple prevents unsupported authority; new records retain complete original tuples.
Library arbitration validates and detaches lease input before backend contact and before the availability catch. Invalid hard and soft requests cannot contact the backend or create launch permission.

Local inbox input is fully validated and detached before physical lock or state creation. Existing alias/getter/toJSON tests now prove captured values remain safe rather than relying on later mutable caller state.

findings.reason: Direct SQL send validates the JSON-representable frozen DATA metadata policy before advisory locking, pruning or normalization. Recursive checks cover keys/strings, nested arrays/objects, encoded JSON, provider-shaped payloads, depth64 and values that would become nonfinite in the JS reader. Valid redacted placeholders, fencingToken, boolean autoRefreshToken and safe ordinary metadata remain admissible. The admitted SQL test uses the shared48 rejected/13 allowed corpus, preserves exact retained inbox digests including future timestamps, exercises timestamp/depth/numeric controls and parses the following complete valid page with the frozen message schema. No exported API, RPC signature, roles, fixture helpers or core contract changes.

A per-call cryptographic private-Unicode namespace preserves exact unsupported UTF16-unit identities in temporary inspection, while valid surrogate pairs stay native. Prior surrogate markers are restored only after deeper-layer JSON syntax admission, then pairs are reassessed before re-encoding. Null/surrogate keys no longer collapse into literal punctuation or each other. Original stored body unchanged. Collision probability follows the declared UUID identity engineering assumption, not a claim of mathematical injectivity. Tests include both null-collision orders, distinct-surrogate/provider-subtree collisions and paired-surrogate/UTF8 last-member aliases.

NUL temporary markers retain nonword/nonwhitespace control characters, keeping an unescaped later JSON layer invalid as in JavaScript. Tests accept twice-encoded actual NUL and escaped-backslash text and compare original bodies exactly.

Nonfinite numeric tokens become a distinct temporary marker rather than immediate refusal. Only surviving markers are rejected after JSONB resolves effective duplicate keys; discarded overflow and escaped-key/pair aliases remain accepted, surviving overflow still rejects without mutation.

COORD R7 repair review — seat: manual tools-enabled Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5) TUI
Source: b9b5d3800fd6b81af7033bc409076c2044a2315d (clone clean, detached HEAD verified)
Delta reviewed: 73443985339ebe18ed78e4e457d3b2c0c8eb15fa..HEAD (source change in 6f27fe3; b9b5d38 is evidence/docs metadata)
Migration digest under review: ab0bf74dcfa1168c5a72083097e7a42c63a5be3db22b14b935adb49881d31d98 (matches COORD-CR-reconciliation-7344398.json source_binding)

BLOCKERS: none.

WHAT I CHECKED
1. Fallback scope and the unchanged normal path
   - supabase/migrations/20260930000000_coordination_server_time.sql:417-454. The only normal-path edit moves `encoded_source := metadata_text` ahead of the
     block. When `::json` succeeds, behaviour is unchanged. 22P02 still means ordinary text (:419). Only class 54 enters the new handler (:420).
   - The handler is reached only for inputs that previously raised an uncaught 54001 (the whole send was refused). So no input the earlier code accepted can now be
     refused. Previously refused deep inputs now get the frozen-TS outcome.
   - Frozen reference: packages/core-contracts/src/redaction.ts:105-131 (depth>64 leak; JSON.parse failure = text). I confirmed that Node 24/V8 JSON.parse is
     iterative: it parses 2,000,000-deep arrays/objects and raises SyntaxError for malformed deep text. The TS side therefore treats valid deep JSON as JSON, which is
     what the SQL fold now mirrors.
   - core-contracts (redaction.ts, coordination-contract.ts) is unchanged versus base b576d92. No signature, privilege, stack-setting or public-limit changes.

2. Grammar validator (:425-452), by code reading
   - Token regex. PostgreSQL ARE alternation is longest-match, so each token is unambiguous:
     - strings exclude raw U+0000-U+001F and accept only valid escapes;
     - numbers follow the JSON grammar;
     - keywords match exactly;
     - whitespace is only space/tab/LF/CR;
     - `.` consumes everything else, so the whole input is tokenised with no gaps.
   - States 1-10 implement value / array / object / key / colon / comma transitions:
     - closers are valid only in 3/5 (`]`) or 6/10 (`}`), so trailing commas, empty-slot commas and mismatched closers are invalid;
     - a final `level=1 and state=2` check rejects incomplete input and anything trailing the root value.
   - The state machine runs over every token, including skipped deep subtrees. Skipping only suppresses appending. A pop below the skip level ends the fold
     without emitting the closer.
   - Folding replaces composites at effective depth metadata_depth+level>64 with to_jsonb(guard_nonfinite). The bounded inspection text is therefore at most
     64 deep, and its `::jsonb` (:488) cannot overflow.
   - A surviving marker is refused by :405 (depth) or :408 (marker). A discarded marker disappears through JSONB last-member resolution, after the
     NUL/surrogate/nonfinite rewrites (:457-487) run on the folded text as before.
   - Lexical checks (:409-414) still scan the original text. The payload is still built from message->'body' (:548-559). All refusals happen before the
     advisory lock / update / delete / insert (:542+).

3. Differential probes. These were small and extracted, and are NOT the full SQL gate.
   - Set-up: a disposable, network-isolated container from the CI-pinned image postgres@sha256:45cd22f8… (PostgreSQL 17.6, max_stack_depth 2MB), already present
     locally. I loaded the exact lines 328-587 plus a probe wrapper that rolls back after confirming the stored body equals the input body.
   - Comparison target: a JS mirror of the frozen scanMetadataLeaks rules.
   - Result: 591 cases, 0 verdict mismatches (388 accept / 203 refuse). Every refusal was 22023, with no stray 54001/22P02. Every accepted body was stored
     unchanged.
   - Coverage:
     - 31 valid and 71 malformed token/structure edges, each placed after the deep member, inside skipped deep arrays, inside skipped deep objects, and inside a
       kept array. The edges include escapes, \/, \u case, raw U+2028/DEL, -0/exponents, 01/1./.1/1e/+1/NaN/Infinity, nul/nulls/truex, raw TAB/LF/0x1F,
       \a/\x/\u12/\U, [,] [1,] [1 2] {"a"} {"a":} {"a":1,} {1:2}, mismatched closers, form-feed / NBSP / BOM / VT "whitespace", comments, trailing garbage and
       multiple roots.
     - Leading and trailing whitespace or garbage.
     - Depth boundaries at string depths 2/30/61/62/63/64 for arrays, objects, scalars and empty composites (effective 64 accepted, 65 refused).
     - Aliases: x vs x in both orders, surrogate case, surrogate pair vs raw astral, NUL keys, \/ vs /, \" vs " and __proto__. Distinct keys stay
       distinct, including NFC vs NFD (no Unicode normalisation, matching JS).
     - The nested encoded-JSON layer, including a deep string inside a fallback document.
     - The prior repairs, inside fallback documents:
       - nonfinite numbers (±1e400, the 1.7976931348623157e308 / …159e308 boundary, overwritten nonfinite);
       - \u0000 and lone surrogates in values and keys;
       - "pass\ud800word" / "password\u0000" sensitive keys.
     - env / provider payload / placeholder cases where the fold lands on "reason" (always refused when the fold survives; never a false acceptance).
     - The test's own malformed variants.
   - Fallback actually exercised: both deep arrays and deep objects raise 54001 under `::json`.
   - json/jsonb stack window: an instrumented, renamed copy found no depth where `::json` succeeds but the unguarded `::jsonb` (:488) overflows. The normal-to-fallback
     transition is clean (arrays ≈16.3k, objects ≈14.5k, mixed ≈7.7k) in 10-level fine scans; 243/243 passed.
   - Cost scales linearly: about 0.46 s at depth 200k, which is cheaper than the existing normal path on large shallow input. 500 KB plain and escape-heavy strings in
     kept and skipped regions behaved correctly.
   - The container was removed. The clone is untouched.

4. Tests and docs
   - tests/guard/coordination.integration.db.test.ts:150-151 and 169 refuse surviving deep valid JSON, the later deep duplicate, and encodedBoundary(61) without
     mutation.
   - :179-181 accept malformed deep text, overwritten and aliased deep members, and encodedBoundary(60). :197-198 cross-check these against the frozen
     coordinationMessageSchema and require the bodies to be unchanged.
   - Statements go to psql via stdin with a 15 s timeout, so there is no argv or timeout artifact.
   - docs/coordination-backend.md:25-28 accurately describes the behaviour.

5. Evidence honesty
   - COORD.json and COORD-closeout.json stay bound to 7344398 / migration f9e7cb68 and make no claim of verification for the R7 source.
   - The reconciliation records the timed-out Opus attempt as unavailable, never as approval.
   - Pending gates are recorded honestly; they are not source defects.

CLASSIFY-LIMIT OWNERSHIP AMENDMENT (plans/phase-plan-v2-COORD.md:111): APPROVE.
packages/cli/src/classify-limit.test.ts:76-80 is the only CLI test edit. The catalog now projects excerpts at publication
(packages/rate-limit-catalog/src/rules.ts:200, used at :540), so the CLI's unchanged sanitizeExcerpt (packages/cli/src/commands/classify-limit.ts:8-23)
receives "[redacted]" and adds no note. The amendment replaces the obsolete note assertion with "[redacted]". It adds stronger no-leak assertions on stdout and
on persisted ledger records. It makes no classifier implementation or public-contract change.

NAMESPACE ASSUMPTION: retained. The fold markers reuse the existing per-call guard_nonfinite marker (122 random bits). A marker can never be a key, never enters
stored bodies (I verified the bodies are unchanged), and any surviving marker sits at depth >64 and is refused anyway.

OPTIONAL SUGGESTIONS (non-blocking)
- Catch `statement_too_complex` (54001) instead of the class name `program_limit_exceeded` (:420), to match the documented "54001 only" design exactly.
  Behaviour is equivalent, because the handler revalidates the whole grammar.
- The normal path's `encoded_text::jsonb` (:488) is unguarded. It is safe only because PERFORM's `::json` overflows first. That held on the pinned 17.6 image, but a
